about.title: Personal Injury Help in Dixon, California
about.longDescription: Dixon sits at a crossroads of daily commuter traffic, with I-80 running through town alongside Rt 113, West A Street, and Pitt School Road carrying a steady mix of local and pass-through drivers. Public records show 77 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 92 people injured and 1 traffic death. Those numbers reflect real people dealing with medical bills, missed work, and recovery — and if that's your situation, you don't have to sort it out alone. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Dixon with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm, we don't handle your case ourselves, and we never charge you anything. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Whether your injury happened on one of Dixon's busier corridors, at an intersection, or somewhere else in Solano County, getting informed early matters — California law gives you a limited window to act, and understanding your options costs nothing. Reach out and we'll help point you toward someone who can look at what happened and explain where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault gets divided.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means what you've been through physically and emotionally can factor into what you're owed.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That structure lets you focus on healing instead of worrying about legal bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Dixon?
items.answer: In most California injury cases you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government entity is involved, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Dixon?
items.answer: Public crash records point to I-80, Rt 113, West A Street, and Pitt School Road as the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts in Dixon, with reported crashes tending to peak on Saturdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free referral service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't represent you directly, and there's never a cost to use our service.
